tasks.title: Group levels
tasks.statement: Group by city and year and print the index level names.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune"], "year": [2026], "v": [1]})
s = df.groupby(["city", "year"])["v"].sum()
print(list(s.index.names))

tasks.title: Category codes
tasks.statement: Store the column as a category and print the integer codes.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["b", "a", "b"], dtype="category")
print(s.cat.codes.tolist())

tasks.title: A parameterised pipe
tasks.statement: Scale the values by 3 through pipe and print the result.

tasks.title: Query with a variable
tasks.statement: Keep values above the local limit and print them.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

limit = 2
df = pd.DataFrame({"v": [1, 2, 3]})
print(df.query("v > @limit")["v"].tolist())

debug.title: A cross-section on a level that is not there

import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune"], "year": [2026], "v": [1]})
s = df.groupby(["city", "year"])["v"].sum()

debug.title: An unordered category sorted alphabetically
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["low", "high"], dtype="category")
print(s.sort_values().tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(pd.Categorical(["low", "high"], categories=["low", "high"], ordered=True))
print(s.sort_values().tolist())
debug.error: Wrong output: ['high', 'low'] — an unordered category sorts by label, not by the intended severity order.

debug.title: int8 overflow that never warns

s = pd.Series([200])

debug.title: A scaler fitted on the held-out row

print(round(float((df.iloc[:3]["x"] - df["x"].mean()).mean()), 1))
debug.fix:

tasks.title: Pass rate per city
tasks.statement: Print learners and pass rate per city rounded to two decimals.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune", "Pune", "Delhi"], "passed": [True, False, True]})
print(df.groupby("city")["passed"].agg(learners="size", rate="mean").round(2).to_dict("index"))

tasks.title: A reproducible sample
tasks.statement: Draw the same sample twice with one seed and print whether they match.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"x": range(6)})
a = df.sample(3, random_state=11)["x"].tolist()
b = df.sample(3, random_state=11)["x"].tolist()
print(a == b)

debug.title: A pass rate computed on attempts
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"user": [1, 1, 2], "passed": [True, False, True]})
print(round(float(df["passed"].mean()), 2))
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"user": [1, 1, 2], "passed": [True, False, True]})

print(round(float(per_user.mean()), 2))
debug.error: Wrong output: 0.67 — that weights the user with two attempts twice, so it is not the per-user pass rate.
